question: What actually limits the savestate epoch generated_bf(N) on the Free-assisted backend, and is the limit address space?
method: 1. Compiling and running generated_bf(N) directly gave a ceiling that looked like 110 and moved with the input state, so it was not a clean capacity number.

2. semantic.differential() compares the Free backend against the independent BFIR1 reference VM on stdout, the whole 256-cell tape and the final pointer. On the unpatched tree it is OK for N<=110 and BackendNotHalted for N>=111.
3. Padding the Brainfuck with semantically inert ',[-]' after all output, holding N=105 fixed, moves the same boundary. So the limit is compiled program length, not tape cells.
4. Boundary search on padding: last OK at 990 compiled cells, first fail at 1004.
5. MalbolgeCore.runWithTrace showed the first bad opcode at c=1000, with cells there holding 0/1 instead of program characters. max_addr for N=111 is 3412 vs 1255 for N=110.
6. The Free core hardcodes the tape base in three places: cellWrite(1000 + tape_index, 0), d = 999, and while (tape_index < 256).
7. Parameterising all three in a /tmp copy of vendor/malfuck (repo untouched) lifts the differential to N=4096.

three_hardcoded_literals.note: semantic.zig also declares TAPE_BASE_ADDR=1000, but that one is only the read-back; changing it alone moved nothing, which is what proved the limit was elsewhere.

evidence_after_patch.status: backend Free == BFIR1 reference on stdout, full 4096-cell tape and final pointer

residual_limit: The compiled program must end below TAPE_BASE. At ~9 program cells per tape cell and TAPE_BASE=10000, N=1024 (9219 cells) passes and N=2048 (18435 cells) collides again; TAPE_BASE=50000 lifts it.
claim: TAPE_SIZE_IS_NOT_THE_LIMIT=DEMONSTRATED. SAVESTATE_EPOCH_TWO_IMPL_PARITY=DEMONSTRATED up to 4096 cells under a parameterised base. SAVESTATE_EPOCH_UNBOUNDED=NOT_DEMONSTRATED, now bounded by TAPE_BASE vs program length rather than by 256.
